reading.rtitle: Minutes -- Weekly export call, Bom Sabor and Lakeshore Foods
paras: Attendees: Roberto Saraiva (chair), Megan Ross and Paula Lima. The call started at nine thirty and finished at nine fifty-five. Roberto opened the meeting and said there were three items on the agenda. He said the delay at the port was the first item, because it affected the other two.

Item 1, the delay at the port. Megan said the container was still in Savannah. She explained that customs wanted one more document. Paula confirmed that the document was ready, and Roberto said his team would send it the same day. Action item: Paula Lima, send the document to customs, Thursday.

Item 2, the price for the third quarter. Megan pointed out that the new price was four percent higher than last quarter. She said she could not decide on price without her director, so this item is on hold until next Thursday. Roberto raised one concern: if the decision takes more than two weeks, the June production will be late. Megan said she understood, and that she would talk to her director on Monday.

Item 3, the samples for the fair. Megan told the team that the samples looked great, and that Lakeshore needed fifty more for the fair. Roberto confirmed that they could ship them by the tenth. Next steps: these minutes are circulated today, and all attendees should reply by Friday if anything is wrong. Next call: Thursday, same time.

listenings.text: Hi, Roberto, it's Megan. I read the minutes, and thank you for sending them so fast. They are almost perfect, but there is one thing I would like to correct. The minutes say I would talk to my director on Monday. Actually, I said I would talk to him on Tuesday, because he is traveling on Monday. It is a small thing, but my director reads these too. And one detail is missing. I said that we needed the fifty samples by the tenth, and that part is right. But I also said they should come with the new labels, not the old ones. Could you add that and circulate the minutes again? Everything else is correct. Talk to you on Thursday.

Here is the mistake I see in almost every set of minutes. People try to write down everything. They write a transcript, and nobody reads a transcript. Good minutes are short, and they answer four questions. Who was there? What did we decide? What is on hold, and until when? And who does what, by when? For the discussion, you do not need every word. You report it. You write: the buyer said the price was too high. Not her full sentence, just the idea. And one more rule. Circulate the minutes the same day. Not tomorrow. Today. If people get them a week later, they remember a different meeting, and then you have two meetings to fix instead of one.
